 By 1News Reporters 12:47pm Close-Up of Man Refueling Vehicle at Gas Station Pump. File photo. (Source: istock.com)
 SHARE ME
 Petrol and diesel prices rose sharply in the 12 months to October, while food costs also increased, according to new data released by Stats NZ. 
 The data released Tuesday showed petrol prices rose 38% while diesel increased 71.2% between October 2025 and October 2026. 
 Fuel prices were up for a third consecutive month in October, with petrol and diesel up 11.9% and 11.1%, respectively, compared to September. 
 The cost of fuel has been unstable since the United States and Israel launched attacks on Iran in February, effectively closing the Strait of Hormuz — a critical global shipping route through which about 20% of the world’s oil exports passed before the war.
 Since February, petrol prices have increased 40.8%, while diesel prices have risen 73%. 
 ADVERTISEMENT Also up was food, increasing 2.3% in the 12 months to October. Restaurant meals and ready-to-eat food (up 3.4%) were the biggest drivers, followed by grocery food (up 2.1%). 
 Onions, chocolate blocks, potatoes, and takeaway coffee recorded increases, with the cost of onions more than doubling over the period. 
 “In October 2025, the average price for a kilogram of onions was $1.76. In October 2026, onions rose to $3.66 a kilogram,” Stats NZ prices and deflators spokesperson Jason Attewell said.
 Price decreases were recorded for fresh eggs, cabbage, and tomatoes.
 While annual food prices rose in October, they dropped 0.4% when compared with September's figures. 
 This was driven by the grocery food group (down 0.9%), followed by fruit and vegetables (down 1.6%). 
 Decreases were recorded for meal kits, tomatoes, capsicums, and cucumbers while increases were recorded for onions, chocolate blocks, boxed chocolates, and porterhouse/sirloin beef.
 ADVERTISEMENT Domestic airfares also rose 33.5% annually in October. 
 “The 33.5% annual increase in domestic airfares was the largest since the year ended April 2023,” Attewell said. 
 Compared with September, airfares rose 13.6% in October. It followed a 9.6% increase the month prior.
